Lukas is asking whether there are plans to support HTTP/2/gRPC so he can include secret injection in an updated guide for his product, letting users rely on secret injection as a more secure integration path.

Visible reaction count (root message): 1 reaction (white check mark emoji).

- More secure usage model: Lukas explicitly says he wants to integrate a section on secret injection in his product guide so users “could use this (which seems to be more secure)” — benefit is letting end-users adopt a more secure secret-handling pattern via Daytona.
- Documentation improvement: After the fix, Lukas says “thank you! will update our docs”, indicating this feature enables better / updated customer docs around Daytona integration.
- Confirmed feature support for HTTP/2/gRPC: Final reply “Seems to work, ty!” after deployment indicates the fix allows secret injection to function in the HTTP/2 / gRPC setting, unlocking real usage in that environment.

Explicitly stated concerns / issues from the thread:
- Lack of HTTP/2/gRPC support: Initial problem statement is that secret injection “doesn’t support http2/grpc”.
- Concrete failure behavior: Lukas shows an example where HTTP/1.1 works but HTTP/2 hangs until timeout; output summary notes: secret substitution works on HTTP/1.1; HTTP/2 (`--http2-prior-knowledge`) times out with no bytes received.
- Production readiness / deployment lag: Later in the thread, Lukas tests again and reports it still doesn’t work with the latest SDK; Dalin clarifies it “hasn’t been deployed yet”, then later says “This got merged” and then “This was deployed, please test now”, indicating a short gap between code merge and production deployment.

- Dalin asks for a code snippet and Lukas shares a detailed TypeScript example showing HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 requests using a Daytona sandbox and secret.
- Dalin confirms an internal issue was filed, that a PR was opened, that it got merged, and then that it was deployed.
- Lukas validates post-deployment that the fix works and confirms he’ll update docs.
